architectural_shifts: Shift from heuristic per-rule search to exact/verified per-rule solvers, then MILP level selection for rank-based rules, then verified boundary polishing; grounded only in solver design, not in model architecture changes. Modest measured solver-efficiency gains: combined score 1.0018 -> 1.0034, all runs verified correct, plan validity rate 1.0.
benchmarks: Open LLM Leaderboard contents/results (IFEval, BBH, MATH Lvl 5, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro)
reference_query_plan.central_topic: How much per-task targeted investment (score boost, measured by L1 depth and breadth over subtasks) a developer needs to make a target model rank first on public multi-task leaderboards (HELM MMLU 57 subjects, Open LLM Leaderboard 6 tasks), and how that minimal cost varies across aggregation rules.
comparators: Computational social choice: bribery, margin of victory, manipulation of voting rules
Social-choice aggregation for multi-task/agent evaluation (Vote'n'Rank, Lanctot et al.)
Benchmark contamination and leaderboard gaming (Leaderboard Illusion, contamination papers)
Robust statistics (trimmed mean, median breakdown point)
core_methods: Minimum-cost boost plan solvers per aggregation rule (exact for mean/median/maximin/plurality; verified heuristics and MILP level selection for trimmed mean/Borda/Copeland/z-score)
Exact-replica verification and verified boundary polishing (bisection shrink, redundant-drop, pairwise transfer) of boost plans
Breadth-constrained cost (number of tasks boosted) vs depth (L1 total boost)
Bootstrap CIs, task-subsampling robustness, Holm/Wilcoxon tests
forbidden_query_patterns: Any query naming or paraphrasing the withheld published paper on this exact research question (title, authors, results), or pages citing/discussing it

queries.query: bribery and margin of victory in voting rules computational complexity
queries.rationale: Minimal targeted boost to make a target rank first is a cost-minimizing manipulation/bribery problem; margin of victory and bribery are the closest formal analogues for the cost-vs-rule comparison (depth L1 cost, breadth cost).

queries.query: manipulation of Borda and Copeland rules complexity
queries.rationale: Borda, Copeland and plurality are the rank-based rules solved by MILP level selection; their manipulation/bribery hardness motivates exact vs heuristic solvers.

queries.query: rank aggregation of multi-task benchmark scores with social choice rules (Borda, Copeland, maximin)
queries.rationale: Comparator literature for the aggregation rules studied (mean, median, trimmed mean, min, Borda, plurality, Copeland); beyond starter items 5 and 11, includes Vote'n'Rank-style benchmark aggregation.

queries.query: robustness of rankings to task selection and aggregation choice in multi-task benchmarks
queries.rationale: Reviewers expect connection to benchmark-lottery/task-sensitivity work: how rule choice changes who is first, which is the baseline for the paper's rule-dependence claim.

queries.query: trimmed mean median robust location estimator breakdown point
queries.rationale: Mean, median and trimmed mean differ in how many per-task boosts are needed; breakdown point/influence function theory explains the predicted cost ordering.

queries.query: benchmark contamination training on test data inflates language model leaderboard scores
queries.rationale: Targeted investment is modeled as including subset-related data in training; contamination/leakage literature supports the plausibility and magnitude of per-task score gains.

queries.query: adaptive overfitting and holdout reuse in machine learning leaderboards
queries.rationale: Strategic targeting of leaderboard components is a form of overfitting to the evaluation; Ladder/holdout-reuse work frames leaderboard gaming and limits of the claims.

queries.query: Open LLM Leaderboard IFEval GPQA MuSR MMLU-Pro BBH MATH benchmark suite
queries.rationale: Scientific context for the 6-task Open LLM Leaderboard data used; the task components need citations.

queries.query: HELM MMLU 57 subjects per-subject scores language model evaluation
queries.rationale: 57-subject HELM MMLU v1.13.0 is the many-task setting; the dataset and evaluation framework need accurate citations.

queries.query: confidence intervals and uncertainty for model rankings on leaderboards bootstrap
queries.rationale: The run reports bootstrap CIs and subsample-task robustness over rankings; ranking-uncertainty literature supports the methodology.

result_driven_themes: Minimal investment depends strongly on aggregation rule (mean vs median vs min vs rank-based rules)
Verified exact/near-exact plans with small gains from polishing over earlier heuristics
Plausibility of targeted gains via data contamination or targeted training
Uncertainty and robustness of conclusions to task subsets and snapshots
